articles.title: Your $180 Coat Sold for $18. One Decimal Point Did That.
articles.excerpt: The best morning of the year lasts ten seconds Black Friday, 6:40 a.m. The phone is buzzing before the alarm. Orders, lots of them. For about ten seconds it feels like the best morning of the year. Th…
articles.body: The best morning of the year lasts ten seconds Black Friday, 6:40 a.m. The phone is buzzing before the alarm. Orders, lots of them. For about ten seconds it feels like the best morning of the year. Then you open one order. The $180 coat sold for $18. A November 2026 account by Emirhan Sönmez, who builds Shopify operations tools, collects this exact failure from real sellers. On r/shopify, a seller wrote that an employee uploaded SKUs with the decimal in the wrong place — items meant for $19.99 sold at $1.99, and the store was shouldering heavy losses. On r/shopify_growth, another seller described a 20%-off CSV update for about 80 products where a formatting issue shifted one column for about 30 rows. A $180 item went live at $18. A $220 item went live at $2.20. It ran for 14 hours.

articles.title: WARN Act and Your Prescription Drug Coverage — What Happens to Your Medications After a Layoff Notice
articles.excerpt: WARN Act and Your Prescription Drug Coverage — What Happens to Your Medications After a Layoff Notice A WARN notice gives you 60 days' warning that your job is ending. For most people, the first worry…
articles.body: WARN Act and Your Prescription Drug Coverage — What Happens to Your Medications After a Layoff Notice A WARN notice gives you 60 days' warning that your job is ending. For most people, the first worry is the paycheck. The second, quieter worry shows up at the pharmacy counter: what happens to the medications you take every day? Here is the reassuring part first. A prescription is a clinician's order to a pharmacy, and losing your job does not cancel it. What ends is your employer's health plan paying for it — and you have more options, and more time, than the notice makes it feel like. As of November 22, 2026, Layoff Atlas tracks 756 WARN notices covering 61,768 reported workers in a 90-day window.

articles.title: From RAG to Reality: Why Verified Retrieval Breaks Under Load (and What to Do Instead)
articles.excerpt: Originally published on tamiz.pro. Verified retrieval has become the default answer to RAG's credibility problem. Instead of trusting a vector store, you make the retriever prove itself: pull the top-…
articles.body: Originally published on tamiz.pro . Verified retrieval has become the default answer to RAG's credibility problem. Instead of trusting a vector store, you make the retriever prove itself: pull the top-k chunks, run them past an LLM judge, discard the irrelevant ones, and only then generate. It works beautifully — at one request per second. At one hundred requests per second, the "verification" that was supposed to save your answers becomes the thing that kills your p99, your token budget, and eventually your whole service. This article is about why that happens and what to build instead: a tiered verification architecture that keeps the quality benefits of Self-RAG and CRAG while surviving real production load. We'll measure the failure, then rebuild the pipeline from first principles. 1.
articles.author: Tamiz Uddin

articles.title: How AI Detectors Work: Why One Essay Can Score 100% and 0%
articles.excerpt: How AI detectors work: each one scores your finished text, not how you wrote it, with its own model and its own line, so one essay can get 100% AI from one detector and 0% from two others. We start wi…
articles.body: How AI detectors work: each one scores your finished text, not how you wrote it, with its own model and its own line, so one essay can get 100% AI from one detector and 0% from two others. We start with a real case: at Adelphi University a professor's report said Turnitin scored an essay 100%, the student said two detectors his parents ran showed 0%, and a New York judge annulled the violation in January 2026, over process and evidence, not detector accuracy. From there we follow the idea: perplexity and burstiness, why GPTZero called part of the US Constitution likely AI in 2023, OpenAI's own classifier (26% of AI text caught in its test, 9% of human writing wrongly flagged, then pulled for low accuracy), and the deep learning models GPTZero and Turnitin describe now.

articles.body: In my last post about rebuilding Eastman Kodak's 1928–1989 13-month calendar for 2027, several readers asked about an unexpected astronomical coincidence: why does 2027 have 13 New Moons, and how do you compute lunar illumination accurately in a static browser app without shipping a 500 KB ephemeris library? Here is the exact pipeline I used for SOL-2027 — combining PyEphem / Jean Meeus UTC tables at build time with a tiny O(1) lookup and cosine phase interpolator in pure JavaScript. articles.body: I'm a beginner in open source, and FactReel is my first project with outside contributors. In the last month three people have sent pull requests, and I learned more from reviewing them than from writing the code myself. Disclosure: I build it with Claude's help and review the result myself. What FactReel does It makes short vertical videos (YouTube Shorts, TikTok, Reels) from a list of facts you provide. An LLM writes the script, but it is only allowed to use the facts you gave it: numbers and dates are checked, rumours are labelled, and if the LLM fails there is a facts-only fallback. Voices and images have free provider chains with an offline fallback.

articles.body: SpaceX launched a batch of classified satellites this morning (Nov. 22), on the NROL-136 mission out of California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base's Launch Complex-4E at 7:23 a.m. ET (1223 GMT; 4:23 a.m. local time in California). It was the sixth National Reconnaissance Office launch (NROL) this year to deliver a payload, or group of payloads, to low Earth orbit , all which have been carried out by SpaceX 's workhorse Falcon 9. The launch marks another step in the NRO's effort to expand its intelligence-gathering capabilities through a proliferated network of spacecraft designed to provide more frequent and timely surveillance of locations around the globe. articles.excerpt: On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. It lifted off from Kennedy Space Center and up into the dark of night. This was the third nighttime launch of the shuttle program and the 32nd shuttle mission overall. Discovery had five astronauts on board. Their mission was to deploy a classified payload for the U.S. Department of Defense. NASA and the military launched several secretive shuttle missions to deploy military satellites . The satellite that launched with STS-33 is believed to be a type of spy satellite called Magnum. But exactly what Magnum was doing in orbit remains classified. articles.title: 10 things that worry me about chasing the 2027 total solar eclipse in Egypt
articles.excerpt: The longest total solar eclipse on land this century promises to be the experience of a lifetime, but watching it from Luxor, Egypt, may not be straightforward. What could go wrong? Quite a lot, actua…
articles.body: On Aug. 2, 2027, I'll be in Luxor, Egypt, to witness what could be the greatest total solar eclipse of my life. I've seen nine total solar eclipses across the world, but this one promises to be different. For a remarkable six minutes and 22 seconds, the moon will completely cover the sun, plunging Egypt's ancient temples and monuments into eerie twilight as the solar corona bursts into view. I've been calling it the "eclipse of the century" for many years, and for good reason. It will be the longest total solar eclipse until 2114 — and the longest on land of the 21st century — and it will take place in one of the most extraordinary places on Earth. What could go wrong? I've chased eclipses long enough to know that the celestial mechanics are the easy part.

articles.body: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 22 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Swirls and Colors on Jupiter from Juno Explanation: What creates the colors in Jupiter’s clouds? No one is sure. The thick atmosphere of Jupiter is mostly hydrogen and helium , elements which are colorless at the low temperatures of the Jovian cloud tops . Which trace molecules provide the colors remains a topic of research , although small amounts of ammonium hydrosulfide are one leading candidate .
